Algebra_Structure.title: Algebra Structure
Algebra_Structure.define: An algebraic structure is a set equipped with operations whose behavior is controlled by specified axioms.

Boolean_Algebra.title: Boolean Algebra
Boolean_Algebra.define: Boolean algebra is an algebraic structure that formalizes logical operations such as and, or, and not.

Chain_Complex.title: Chain Complex
Chain_Complex.define: A chain complex is a sequence of modules or vector spaces linked by differentials whose successive composition is zero.

Complex_Field.title: Complex Field
Complex_Field.define: The complex field extends the real numbers by adjoining a square root of $-1$.

Cubic_Function.title: Cubic Function
Cubic_Function.define: A cubic function is a polynomial function whose highest-degree term has degree three.

Differential_Manifold.title: Differential Manifold
Differential_Manifold.define: A smooth manifold is a space that locally looks like $\mathbb R^n$, and whose overlapping coordinate systems transform smoothly into one another.

Field.title: Field
Field.define: A field is an algebraic structure where addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by nonzero elements are all possible.

Fourth_Order_Function.title: Fourth Order Function
Fourth_Order_Function.define: A fourth-order function is a polynomial function whose highest-degree term has degree four.

Function.title: Function
Function.define: A function assigns each input exactly one output.

Group.title: Group
Group.define: A group is an algebraic structure that captures reversible composition with an identity element.

Inner_Product_Space.title: Inner Product Space
Inner_Product_Space.define: An inner product space is a vector space with a product that defines length, angle, and orthogonality.

Lattice.title: Lattice
Lattice.define: A lattice is an ordered set in which every pair of elements has both a greatest lower bound and a least upper bound.

Lie_Algebra.title: Lie Algebra
Lie_Algebra.define: A Lie algebra is a vector space equipped with a bilinear bracket satisfying antisymmetry and the Jacobi identity.

Lie_Group.title: Lie Group
Lie_Group.define: A Lie group is a group whose operations vary smoothly with respect to a manifold structure.

Linear_Function.title: Linear Function
Linear_Function.define: A linear function preserves addition and scalar multiplication.

Linear_Space.title: Linear Space
Linear_Space.define: A linear space is a set whose elements can be added and scaled by elements of a field.

Linear_Transformation.title: Linear Transformation
Linear_Transformation.define: A linear transformation is a structure-preserving map between vector spaces.

Manifold.title: Manifold
Manifold.define: A manifold is a space that may be globally curved or complicated but locally looks like Euclidean space.

Module.title: Module
Module.define: A module is a vector-space-like structure whose scalars come from a ring rather than necessarily from a field.

Normed_Linear_Space.title: Normed Linear Space
Normed_Linear_Space.define: A normed linear space is a vector space equipped with a norm that measures vector length.

Polynomial_Function.title: Polynomial Function
Polynomial_Function.define: A polynomial function is a function formed from powers of a variable using finitely many additions and scalar multiplications.

Quadratic_Function.title: Quadratic Function
Quadratic_Function.define: A quadratic function is a polynomial function whose highest-degree term has degree two.

Quaternion_Ring.title: Quaternion Ring
Quaternion_Ring.define: The quaternion ring extends complex numbers with three imaginary units whose multiplication is noncommutative.

Rational_Number_Field.title: Rational Number Field
Rational_Number_Field.define: The rational number field consists of ratios of integers with nonzero denominator under ordinary arithmetic.

Real_Field.title: Real Field
Real_Field.define: The real field is the complete ordered field that models the continuous number line.

Ring.title: Ring
Ring.define: A ring is an algebraic structure with addition, subtraction, and multiplication, where multiplication need not be commutative or invertible.

Sequence.title: Sequence
Sequence.define: A sequence is a function whose domain is usually the natural numbers, listing objects in order.

Set.title: Set
Set.define: A set is a collection of distinct objects considered as a single mathematical object.

Tensor.title: Tensor
Tensor.define: A tensor is a multilinear object that generalizes scalars, vectors, covectors, and linear maps.
